title: Kentucky Public Universities: ADA Title II PDF Accessibility, 5 Measured | SignalFeed.dev
description: How Kentucky public universities stand on PDF accessibility before the April 26, 2027 ADA Title II date: 39% of 254 sampled PDFs untagged, 7% scanned. Aggregate, automated signals.
h1: Kentucky: Title II PDF backlog at public universities
body:
Kentucky has 7 public 4-year universities with 5,000+ students in the federal IPEDS directory. Public universities are covered by the ADA Title II web rule (28 CFR part 35, subpart H), and most are part of state government, which puts them on the April 26, 2027 compliance date. Web content, PDFs included, must conform to WCAG 2.1 Level AA, subject to the rule's exceptions.

Does ADA Title II apply to Kentucky?

Yes. Title II is federal law and covers Kentucky's state agencies and public universities, counties, cities, towns, school districts and special districts; the PDF guide covers the rule's exceptions and dates. This is general information, not legal advice.

We measured the PDFs these institutions link from their main websites. This page summarizes Kentucky as a whole. It does not name or rank individual institutions. See the national university page for the method.

Kentucky at a glance

  • 5 of 7 institutions measured with a usable sample (20 or more PDFs). Of the rest, 0 blocked our crawler and 2 could not be sampled: too few PDFs on the main site (some host documents on other systems) or a crawl that only partly finished. That is not a clean result.
  • 254 PDFs analyzed. 38.6% had no accessibility tags, higher than the national figure of 26.7%. 7.1% were scanned images with no usable text, 50.4% did not declare a document language, and 46% had no document title.
  • Spread: at none of the 5 measured institutions more than half the sampled PDFs were untagged; at none, fewer than 1 in 10 were. The most common main issue was missing accessibility tags (3 of 5 institutions).
  • 0 of 15 sampled PDFs passed the veraPDF PDF/UA-1 checks.
  • The median measured institution has roughly 1,400 pages of PDFs failing at least one basic check; across the measured institutions that is on the order of 27,000 pages.
  • 35% of the sampled PDFs were modified in 2024 or later. Recent documents are more likely to still be in active use, and documents used to apply for, access or participate in a service are not covered by the rule's exception for preexisting documents.

What this means for a Kentucky university

An untagged PDF gives a screen reader no headings, reading order or table structure, and a scanned one gives it nothing; both typically fail WCAG 2.1 AA and are common in catalogs, policies, forms and board materials. Archived content and preexisting documents are exempt unless people use them to get a service, so the usual order is: fix export settings, remediate forms and service documents, then move true archives to a marked archive section. Our ADA Title II PDF guide walks through it.

What this is, and what it isn't

These are automated signals scaled from samples, not a conformance evaluation: a check can show a PDF fails, not that it conforms. Method: national Backlog Index page.

Per-institution data

The Kentucky workbook lists every targeted public university in the state, with PDFs found and estimated, untagged and scanned shares, recent-document share, estimated pages failing basic checks and days to the compliance date. It is built for remediation firms, consultants and agencies planning work.

Per-institution rows for Kentucky are available on request: email us.
